correctness.rationale: Under strictly positive C3 curvature and positive C1 sampling density, the normal intercept of the chord joining nearest clockwise/counterclockwise samples is D(U,V)=kappa UV/2+O(UV(U+V)). For n iid boundary samples the exact nearest-gap joint density is n(n-1)f(z+a)f(z-b)[1-mass(-b,a)]^(n-2) on the short-arc domain. Its n f(z) rescaling converges in L1 by pointwise density convergence plus total mass (Scheffe), hence total variation to independent unit exponentials. For finitely many fixed separated sites, the disjoint-arc joint density with falling factorial (n)_{2m} yields independent pairs. The exposure flag reduces asymptotically to uv>x, a continuous-law threshold, and TV of the joint mark follows from dominated convergence of density and vanishing disagreement mass. Integrating yields H(x)=int_0^inf exp(-u-x/u)du=2sqrt(x)K1(2sqrt(x)). I independently checked this exact integral numerically at three positive depths; derivatives, endpoints and critical scaling follow from monotonicity. Conditional-TV convergence needs H(x)>0, which holds for all fixed t>0. The n^-2 regimes explicitly require depth->0 and fixed-site separation.
